facts.raw_span: A 42-year-old man with 30 pack-years of smoking
cannabis use, alcohol dependence, and the use of herbal products for addiction cessation
presented with a 3-day history of acute urinary retention
hematemesis
progressive neurological deficits
marked paraparesis of the lower limbs (muscle strength 2/5)
hyperreflexia with sustained clonus in the lower extremities
hypertonic sphincters and hyperalgesia
febrile
clear cerebrospinal fluid without albuminocytologic dissociation
glucose 0.49 g/L, protein 0.20 g/L, chloride 121 mmol/L, 14 white blood cells (70% lymphocytes), and 14 red blood cells per mm³
multiple bilateral, symmetrical T2/FLAIR hyperintense lesions in the periventricular and periaqueductal regions

concepts.why: The patient presented with acute urinary retention, marked paraparesis of the lower limbs, hyperreflexia with sustained clonus, and hypertonic sphincters, which are consistent with acute transverse myelitis.
The patient's progressive neurological deficits, multiple bilateral symmetrical T2/FLAIR hyperintense lesions, and normal sensory function are consistent with multiple sclerosis.
The patient's history of substance abuse, febrile state, and abnormal cerebrospinal fluid findings are consistent with toxic encephalopathy.
The patient's marked paraparesis, hyperreflexia, and bilateral symmetrical T2/FLAIR hyperintense lesions are consistent with neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder.
The patient's febrile state, abnormal cerebrospinal fluid findings, and multiple bilateral symmetrical T2/FLAIR hyperintense lesions are consistent with viral meningoencephalitis.

aliases: Subacute Combined Degeneration of the Spinal Cord
concepts.why: The patient's acute urinary retention, marked paraparesis, hyperreflexia, and hypertonic sphincters are consistent with subacute combined degeneration.
The patient's progressive neurological deficits, multiple bilateral symmetrical T2/FLAIR hyperintense lesions, and abnormal cerebrospinal fluid findings are consistent with CNS vasculitis.
The patient's history of substance abuse, febrile state, and abnormal cerebrospinal fluid findings are consistent with toxic neuropathy.
